title: The Canadian pianist who told Zutty he wasn't swinging
summary: Waters tells a funny story of a young stride pianist in Coleman's band telling Zutty Singleton 'you ain't swinging me', to which Zutty replied in kind; Schaap's guesses at his name fail.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah, and then we got to somebody else, I forget who it was now. And then finally that's where you have a little guy from Canada, the negro, Canada that's playing piano. And there was something happening that I never get, didn't, never did get through laughing. One night he was -
That didn't sound like the name. A little bit tall, dark guy, I forget his name now -
Young, kinda young in that period -
No, that don't seem to be that. I don't, he was new to me, see. Anyway he was playing stride, playing like good piano, you know -

So he kept on givin', turning back and lookin' at Zutty. So finally he says "Hey, man, you ain't swingin' me", that's what he told Zutty. So Zutty says "And you ain't swingin' me either". (laughs) I never did stop laughin', all that's goin' on around this place. I laughed like ever about that, I never did forget that -
